items.quote: They came the same evening and found the leak behind the dishwasher.
items.name: Dana R.

items.question: What counts as a plumbing emergency?
items.answer: Water you cannot stop at a fixture valve, a burst or leaking pipe, sewage backing up, or no water at all. Turn off the main water valve first if you can find it.

items.question: Where is my main water shut-off valve?
items.answer: In most homes it sits where the water line comes through the foundation, often in the basement near the water meter.

items.question: Do you clean kitchen drains and main lines?
items.answer: Yes. We clear kitchen, bathroom and main sewer lines.

items.question: Why does my drain keep clogging?
items.answer: Grease, food scraps, hair and soap build up inside pipes over time. Roots can also enter older main lines through small cracks.

items.question: Should I use chemical drain cleaners?
items.answer: They often clear only part of a clog, and strong chemicals can damage older pipes. A cable or a camera check finds the real cause.

items.question: Do you install tank and tankless water heaters?
items.answer: Yes, both. We repair and replace them too.

items.question: How long does a tank water heater last?
items.answer: Many last about eight to twelve years. Hard water, sediment and how often it is drained affect its life.

items.question: What are signs a water heater is failing?
items.answer: Rusty or cloudy hot water, rumbling or popping sounds, water around the base, or hot water that runs out sooner than it used to.

content.heading: A leak or a slow drain?
content.body: Call us or send the form, and we give you a price first.

content.heading: What it involves
content.body: A burst pipe or a running leak can release a lot of water in a short time. The first step is always to shut off the water at the main valve or at the fixture. A plumber then finds the damaged section, replaces it and checks the joints nearby.

included.text: Water on the floor or ceiling
A sudden drop in water pressure
The sound of running water when every tap is off
A damp patch that keeps growing

items.question: Should I turn off the water?
items.answer: Yes. Turn off the main valve to stop the leak while you wait.

items.question: Can a frozen pipe burst?
items.answer: Yes. Water expands as it freezes and can split the pipe.

items.question: Is a small drip urgent?
items.answer: A steady drip wastes water and can rot wood or grow mould over time, so fix it soon.

content.heading: Talk to a plumber
content.body: Call or send the form and we will give you a price first.

content.heading: What it involves
content.body: Drains slow down when grease, hair, soap and food build up inside the pipe. A cable or a water jet clears the line, and a camera can show what caused the clog. Main lines can also be blocked by roots that enter old pipes through small cracks.

included.text: Bad smells from a sink or floor drain
Water backing up in a lower drain

items.question: Why do several drains back up at once?
items.answer: That usually points to a blockage in the main line, not in one fixture.

items.question: Do chemical cleaners fix clogs?
items.answer: They often clear only part of a clog and can harm older pipes.

items.question: How can I keep drains clear?
items.answer: Keep grease and food scraps out of the sink and use strainers in showers.

content.heading: Talk to a plumber
content.body: Call or send the form and we will give you a price first.

content.heading: What it involves
content.body: A tank heater keeps a store of hot water ready; a tankless heater heats water as it flows. Sediment from hard water settles in tanks and makes them work harder. Draining a tank now and then helps it last longer.

included.text: Rumbling or popping from the tank
Water around the base of the heater
Hot water that runs out sooner than before

items.question: How long does a water heater last?
items.answer: Many tank heaters last about eight to twelve years.

items.question: Is tankless better?
items.answer: It saves space and heats on demand; a tank costs less to put in. The right one depends on the home.

items.question: Why is my hot water rusty?
items.answer: Rust can come from corrosion inside the tank or from the pipes.
